correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the Parseval normalization for f_a(d)=p^{-1/2} exp(2πida/p) over the nonzero squares, for every prime p≥7, p≡3(mod4). Quadratic Gauss evaluation yields H_ab=-1+i√p χ(b-a), and G_B=((p-1)I+H)/(2p). Checked the source verifier implements exact integer-polynomial 4x4 determinants for T/O/I/S and resulting P_T/P_O/P_S, not a merely numerical loop. Double regularity with d=(p−1)/2 and t=(p−3)/4 counts each class: n_T=p(p−1)(p−3)(p−7)/64, n_O=n_I=p(p−1)(p−3)(p+1)/192, n_S=p(p−1)(p−3)(p+1)/64. P_T−P_S=16p(y−1) and P_O−P_S=8p(y+p−1) imply the largest root is uniquely of type S; y_S<p+1 by positivity and quartic comparison, so the minimum retained lower bound is (p+1−y_S)/(2p)>0. At p=7 type T is absent, but S occurs. Enumerations at finitely many primes confirm, not prove, the universal statement. No scientific contradiction found.
